added_lemmas.statement:
Write the observed summary in the nonredundant chart
\[
b=\bigl(\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_{J-1},(p_x,r_{0,x},r_{1,x})_{x\in\mathcal X}\bigr)\in\mathbb R^{4J-1},
\qquad
\lambda_J=1-\sum_{x<J}\lambda_x,
\]
and write \(\gamma=(\Gamma_A,\Gamma_0,\Gamma_1)\).  Let \((b_0,\gamma_0)\) have strictly positive observed cells and finite budgets, let \(\gamma_0\) be an interior point of \(\mathcal B\cap(1,\infty)^3\), and suppose \(L(b_0,\gamma_0)=0\).  Assume that, on a neighborhood of \((b_0,\gamma_0)\), the legal-candidate system used by \(\mathsf{CERT}\) and stratified by \(\mathsf{ATLAS}\) has one unique active branch for \(L\), represented by an analytic objective \(\phi(z,b,\gamma)\) and analytic equations \(F(z,b,\gamma)=0\), where \(z\in\mathbb R^d\); at its solution \(z_0\), assume that \(F_z(z_0,b_0,\gamma_0)\) is invertible, every denominator is nonzero, every inactive inequality is strict, and the branch is strictly separated in objective value from all inactive candidates.  Define
\[
\dot L_b=\phi_b-\phi_zF_z^{-1}F_b,
\qquad
\dot L_\gamma=\phi_\gamma-\phi_zF_z^{-1}F_\gamma,
\]
with all derivatives evaluated at \((z_0,b_0,\gamma_0)\), and assume \(\dot L_\gamma\neq0\).  For independent observations \(O_i=(X_i,A_i,Y_i)\sim P_{\mathrm{obs}}\), suppose an estimator \(\widehat b_n\) obeys
\[
\sqrt n(\widehat b_n-b_0)
=n^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^n\psi(O_i)+o_P(1)
\ \Longrightarrow\ Z\sim N(0,\Sigma),
\qquad
E\{\psi(O_i)\}=0,
\qquad
E\|\psi(O_i)\|^2<\infty.
\]
Then
\[
\sqrt n\{L(\widehat b_n,\gamma_0)-L(b_0,\gamma_0)\}
\ \Longrightarrow\ \dot L_bZ
\sim N(0,\sigma_L^2),
\qquad
\sigma_L^2=\dot L_b\Sigma\dot L_b^{\mathsf T}.
\]
Let \(\nu_0=\dot L_\gamma^{\mathsf T}/\|\dot L_\gamma\|\), and let \(t_n\) be the unique local solution of
\[
L(\widehat b_n,\gamma_0+t_n\nu_0)=0.
\]
Then \(t_n=O_P(n^{-1/2})\) and
\[
\sqrt n\,t_n
\ \Longrightarrow\
-\frac{\dot L_bZ}{\|\dot L_\gamma\|}
\sim N\!\left(0,\frac{\sigma_L^2}{\|\nabla_\gamma L(b_0,\gamma_0)\|^2}\right).
\]
Thus the root-\(n\) standard-error constant for normal displacement of the regular zero-tipping frontier \(\mathfrak T_0(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\) is exactly \(\sigma_L/\|\nabla_\gamma L\|\).  If \(\sigma_L>0\), consistent plug-in estimators of \(\Sigma\), \(\dot L_b\), and \(\dot L_\gamma\) give the usual pointwise normal confidence interval for this normal coordinate.  The same conclusions hold for \(R\) after replacing \(L\), its active minimizing branch, and its derivatives by \(R\), its active maximizing branch, and its derivatives.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
The strict observed-cell conditions put \(b_0\) in the relative interior of its finite-dimensional probability chart, while the finite interior budget condition permits two-sided perturbations of \(\gamma_0\).  The hypotheses concerning denominators and inactive inequalities ensure that every displayed analytic expression is defined on a neighborhood of \((z_0,b_0,\gamma_0)\).  The unique active branch and its strict objective separation imply on a possibly smaller neighborhood that
\[
F\{z(b,\gamma),b,\gamma\}=0,
\qquad
L(b,\gamma)=\phi\{z(b,\gamma),b,\gamma\}.
\tag{1}
\]
This is precisely the regular legal-candidate regime singled out by \(\mathsf{CERT}\) and the semialgebraic stratification of \(\mathsf{ATLAS}\).

We first derive, rather than assume, the derivative formula.  Put \(h=(h_b,h_\gamma)\) and \(\Delta z=z(b_0+h_b,\gamma_0+h_\gamma)-z_0\).  Analyticity and the first identity in (1) give
\[
0=F_z\Delta z+F_bh_b+F_\gamma h_\gamma
+o\bigl(\|\Delta z\|+\|h\|\bigr).
\tag{2}
\]
Because \(F_z\) is invertible, there is \(c>0\) such that \(\|F_zv\|\geq c\|v\|\) for every \(v\in\mathbb R^d\).  Applying this inequality to (2) and shrinking the neighborhood so that the remainder coefficient multiplying \(\|\Delta z\|\) is at most \(c/2\) yields \(\|\Delta z\|=O(\|h\|)\).  Substitution back into (2), followed by multiplication by \(F_z^{-1}\), gives
\[
\Delta z=-F_z^{-1}F_bh_b-F_z^{-1}F_\gamma h_\gamma+o(\|h\|).
\tag{3}
\]
Expanding the second identity in (1) and using (3) gives, equation by equation,
\[
\begin{aligned}
L(b_0+h_b,\gamma_0+h_\gamma)-L(b_0,\gamma_0)
&=\phi_z\Delta z+\phi_bh_b+\phi_\gamma h_\gamma+o(\|h\|)\\
&=\bigl(\phi_b-\phi_zF_z^{-1}F_b\bigr)h_b
+\bigl(\phi_\gamma-\phi_zF_z^{-1}F_\gamma\bigr)h_\gamma
+o(\|h\|)\\
&=\dot L_bh_b+\dot L_\gamma h_\gamma+o(\|h\|).
\end{aligned}
\tag{4}
\]
Thus \(L\) is differentiable on this branch with the derivatives claimed in the statement.

The assumed asymptotically linear representation implies \(\widehat b_n-b_0=O_P(n^{-1/2})\).  Taking \(h_b=\widehat b_n-b_0\) and \(h_\gamma=0\) in (4), and recalling that \(L(b_0,\gamma_0)=0\), gives
\[
\sqrt nL(\widehat b_n,\gamma_0)
=\dot L_b\sqrt n(\widehat b_n-b_0)+o_P(1)
\ \Longrightarrow\ \dot L_bZ.
\tag{5}
\]
Since \(Z\sim N(0,\Sigma)\), the scalar \(\dot L_bZ\) is centered normal with variance
\[
\operatorname{Var}(\dot L_bZ)=\dot L_b\Sigma\dot L_b^{\mathsf T}=\sigma_L^2,
\tag{6}
\]
which proves the endpoint limit.

It remains to derive the frontier displacement.  By definition of \(\nu_0\),
\[
\dot L_\gamma\nu_0=\|\dot L_\gamma\|>0.
\tag{7}
\]
Continuity of the branch derivative therefore makes the scalar map \(t\mapsto L(b,\gamma_0+t\nu_0)\) strictly increasing for \((b,t)\) sufficiently close to \((b_0,0)\).  Equation (5) shows that its value at \(t=0\) is \(O_P(n^{-1/2})\).  Applying (4) at \(t=\pm M_n n^{-1/2}\), where \(M_n\to\infty\) and \(M_n=o(\sqrt n)\), shows with probability tending to one that the two values have opposite signs.  Continuity and strict monotonicity consequently give a unique root \(t_n\) between them.  The mean-value bound following from (7) first gives \(t_n=O_P(n^{-1/2})\).  Using \(h_b=\widehat b_n-b_0\) and \(h_\gamma=t_n\nu_0\) in (4) then gives
\[
0=\dot L_b(\widehat b_n-b_0)+\|\dot L_\gamma\|t_n+o_P(n^{-1/2}).
\tag{8}
\]
Multiplying (8) by \(\sqrt n\), solving for \(\sqrt n t_n\), and applying (5) yields
\[
\sqrt n\,t_n
=-\frac{\dot L_b\sqrt n(\widehat b_n-b_0)}{\|\dot L_\gamma\|}+o_P(1)
\ \Longrightarrow\
-\frac{\dot L_bZ}{\|\dot L_\gamma\|}.
\tag{9}
\]
Equations (6) and (9) give variance \(\sigma_L^2/\|\dot L_\gamma\|^2\) and hence standard-error constant \(\sigma_L/\|\nabla_\gamma L\|\).  When \(\sigma_L>0\), consistency of the three plug-in quantities and the continuous mapping theorem give the stated pointwise normal interval.  Replacing the active minimum by the active maximum changes none of (1)--(9), proving the assertion for \(R\).

proposed_statement_changes.proposed: Writing \(\gamma=(\Gamma_A,\Gamma_0,\Gamma_1)\), construct from \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{inf}}\) a confidence region for \(\mathfrak T_0(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\cap\mathcal B\) that is asymptotically honest uniformly along sequences approaching finite optimizer ties, legal-root collisions, and positive-dimensional stationary continua.  For every singular stratum at which the first nonzero normal term of the active lower-endpoint algebraic germ has contact order \(k\geq1\), determine the sharp local Hausdorff rate, weak limit, and leading constant, including the Gaussian minimum over tied branches and root birth or death at even \(k\).  The unique nondegenerate \(k=1\) branch with \(\nabla_\gamma L\neq0\) is excluded because it is settled by Theorem \(\mathrm{thm{:}regular\text{-}tipping\text{-}inference}\).
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The old question incorrectly leaves the regular unique-branch case unresolved.  The regular theorem proves its pointwise normal-displacement law and exact standard-error constant.  The honest residual problem is the uniformly valid set-valued law at ties, collisions, continua, and higher-order algebraic contacts.

proposed.name: Regular-branch and singular-frontier inference handle
proposed.construction:
Let \(b=(\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_{J-1},(p_x,r_{0,x},r_{1,x})_{x\in\mathcal X})\) be a nonredundant observed-summary chart and let \(\gamma=(\Gamma_A,\Gamma_0,\Gamma_1)\).  The handle \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{inf}}\) takes an asymptotically linear estimator \(\widehat b_n\), the legal active equations \(F(z,b,\gamma)=0\) and objective \(\phi(z,b,\gamma)\) used by \(\mathsf{CERT}\) or selected on a stratum of \(\mathsf{ATLAS}\), and a covariance estimator.  On a unique legal branch with invertible \(F_z\), nonzero denominators, strict inactive inequalities, strict objective separation, and \(\nabla_\gamma L\neq0\), it computes
\[
\dot L_b=\phi_b-\phi_zF_z^{-1}F_b,
\qquad
\dot L_\gamma=\phi_\gamma-\phi_zF_z^{-1}F_\gamma,
\qquad
\sigma_L^2=\dot L_b\Sigma\dot L_b^{\mathsf T},
\]
and reports the pointwise normal-displacement standard-error constant \(\sigma_L/\|\dot L_\gamma\|\); it applies the analogous formulas to \(R\).  At a finite tie it records the minimum, or maximum, of the tied branch derivatives as the pointwise directional derivative.  It makes no claim of uniform coverage at optimizer ties, legal-root collisions, positive-dimensional stationary continua, or higher-order algebraic contacts; constructing such a procedure and determining its local Hausdorff law remain the singular-frontier open problem.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The frozen handle promises derivative-aware inversion without recording the regularity conditions under which it is proved and treats stationary continua as if replacing a finite active set by a support functional already delivered uniform inference.  This replacement records the proved regular formula and leaves singular uniformity open.

proposed.statement: Writing \(\gamma=(\Gamma_A,\Gamma_0,\Gamma_1)\), construct from \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{inf}}\) a confidence region for \(\mathfrak T_0(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\cap\mathcal B\) that is asymptotically honest uniformly along sequences approaching finite optimizer ties, legal-root collisions, and positive-dimensional stationary continua.  For every singular stratum at which the first nonzero normal term of the active lower-endpoint algebraic germ has contact order \(k\geq1\), determine the sharp local Hausdorff rate, weak limit, and leading constant, including the Gaussian minimum over tied branches and root birth or death at even \(k\).  The unique nondegenerate \(k=1\) branch with \(\nabla_\gamma L\neq0\) is excluded because it is settled by Theorem \(\mathrm{thm{:}regular\text{-}tipping\text{-}inference}\).
proposed.justification: Regular-branch uncertainty is now explicit, but scientifically relevant sign frontiers can switch active optimizers or acquire higher-order contact, where pointwise normal intervals are not uniformly honest.
proposed.gap: Generic directional delta methods identify fixed-law directional limits, but the remaining problem requires a uniform set-valued expansion of moving algebraic active sets and sharp Hausdorff laws at contact order \(k\).
proposed.consumer: Investigators need a simultaneous region for all confounding budgets preserving the sign conclusion, including sequences near ties, root collisions, and stationary continua.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The regular branch is now a proved theorem, so the open question and its dependency graph must isolate only singular uniform inference.

open_obligations.what_is_open: Construct a uniformly honest confidence region for the zero-tipping frontier and determine the sharp local Hausdorff rate, weak limit, and leading constant at finite optimizer ties, legal-root collisions, positive-dimensional stationary continua, and algebraic contact order \(k\geq2\).
open_obligations.obstruction: At a singular stratum the active feasible correspondence moves with the observed law.  A tie produces a Gaussian minimum over several germs; a collision changes the legal-root inventory; a continuum produces a Gaussian support functional indexed by a semialgebraic set; and even-order contact can create or destroy real roots.  The frozen primitives provide neither a uniform stochastic expansion of this moving correspondence nor the anti-concentration and set-inversion bounds needed for honest Hausdorff coverage.
open_obligations.attempted: Implicit differentiation and the asymptotically linear expansion close the unique nondegenerate branch.  Finite-minimum algebra gives the pointwise derivative at a fixed tie, and balancing a fixed order-\(k\) germ against root-\(n\) noise gives the candidate scale \(n^{-1/(2k)}\).  These arguments fail to control local sequences on which branches merge, disappear, or become a continuum.
open_obligations.partial_result:
Theorem \(\mathrm{thm{:}regular\text{-}tipping\text{-}inference}\) proves the \(k=1\) unique-branch law
\[
\sqrt n\,t_n\Longrightarrow
-\frac{\dot L_bZ}{\|\nabla_\gamma L\|},
\qquad
\operatorname{se}_{\sqrt n}(t_n)=\frac{\sigma_L}{\|\nabla_\gamma L\|}.
\]
For finitely many analytic branches \(L_j\) tied at a fixed point, the elementary finite-minimum expansion gives \(L'(h)=\min_{j\in I}\nabla L_j^{\mathsf T}h\), with a maximum in place of a minimum for an upper endpoint.  For one fixed scalar germ \(L(b_0,\gamma_0+t\nu)=ct^k+o(|t|^k)\), \(c\neq0\), balanced against an \(n^{-1/2}\) stochastic perturbation, the only possible nondegenerate displacement scale is \(n^{-1/(2k)}\), and any pointwise candidate limit must solve \(cs^k+G=0\).  These pointwise calculations do not establish uniform Hausdorff coverage, select among several moving tied germs, or handle disappearance of real roots when \(k\) is even.

prose_updates.tldr: For binary treatment and outcome, one shared latent binary confounder, and finite categorical \(X\), the paper derives the exact ATE interval over its own closed common-confounder odds-budget class.  Binary-logistic formulas provide coordinates for the strictly positive chart, but the class is not attributed wholesale to Rosenbaum--Rubin.  A unique quadratic-mixture root reduces each outcome budget to two analytic branches, and both arms optimize over the same posterior pair.  Constructive closure laws prove sharpness; exact fixed-input and parametric semialgebraic procedures certify endpoints and the zero-tipping surface.  A complete deterministic rational artifact certifies strict tightening over the internal separate-pair relaxation.  On a unique nondegenerate active branch, the estimated tipping frontier has an explicit root-\(n\) normal-displacement law with standard-error constant \(\sigma_L/\|\nabla_\gamma L\|\); uniform Hausdorff inference at ties, root collisions, stationary continua, and higher-order contacts remains open.

project_justification.gap: Rosenbaum and Rubin analyze a binary-\(U\), binary-response logistic sensitivity calculation at fixed parameter tuples.  The cited sections do not state this paper's union over arm-specific two-sided outcome-odds budgets, unrestricted coupling of the two potential outcomes, finite-simplex closure, or optimization over one common posterior pair.  Contemporary propensity-only, arbitrary-confounder, and exposure-standardized models likewise do not provide this common-pair envelope.  Existing directional methods do not by themselves give uniformly honest Hausdorff inference when the certified algebraic active set changes dimension or contact order.
project_justification.niche: The maintained class is low dimensional and scientifically calibratable while preserving cross-arm compatibility that separate armwise relaxations discard.  Its semialgebraic geometry supports exact population endpoints, a reproducible strict-gap witness, a multibudget tipping frontier, and an explicit regular-branch sampling law.
project_justification.fill: The paper proves the sharp interval for its stated common-binary-confounder class, records only a binary-logistic coordinate equivalence and fixed-tuple recovery relative to Rosenbaum--Rubin, supplies exact fixed-input and parametric algebraic procedures, and certifies strict internal-relaxation tightening with a complete deterministic artifact and continuity of optimized values.  It also proves pointwise regular tipping inference and isolates uniform singular-frontier inference as a precise open problem.

sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Use a nonredundant empirical-frequency or asymptotically linear estimator of \((\lambda_x,p_x,r_{0,x},r_{1,x})_{x\in\mathcal X}\).  On a unique nondegenerate active branch, implicit differentiation of the certified equations gives the pointwise Gaussian endpoint and normal-frontier limits.  Uniform inference through optimizer ties, legal-root collisions, stationary continua, and higher-order algebraic contacts remains open.

prose_updates.related_work: Rosenbaum and Rubin \cite{RosenbaumRubin1983Sensitivity} study binary \(U\) and binary response through fixed treatment and response logistic sensitivity parameters and recalculate adjusted response rates at a fixed tuple.  This paper uses that fixed-tuple algebraic coordinate calculation only; it does not call its bounded arm-specific odds-budget union, unrestricted potential-outcome coupling, or finite-simplex closure the published Rosenbaum--Rubin class.  VanderWeele and Arah \cite{VanderWeeleArah2011Bias} provide the bias-decomposition identity motivating the arm-mean map.  Ciocănea-Teodorescu, Gabriel, and Sjölander \cite{CiocaneaGabrielSjolander2022Marginal} use variation-independent exposure-standardization sensitivity parameters, while Ding and VanderWeele \cite{DingVanderWeele2016WithoutAssumptions} derive an arbitrary-\(U\) relative-risk factor.  Tan \cite{Tan2006MarginalSensitivity}, Yadlowsky et al. \cite{YadlowskyEtAl2022Bounds}, and Dorn and Guo \cite{DornGuo2023QuantileBalancing} restrict latent treatment odds without this simultaneous common-binary treatment-and-outcome odds geometry.  These published models are generally non-nested with the present class, so the strict comparison in this paper is only with its internal separate-posterior-pair relaxation.  Masten and Poirier \cite{MastenPoirier2020BreakdownFrontier} motivate assumption-frontier inference; Fang and Santos \cite{FangSantos2019InferenceDirectional} provide generic pointwise directional theory; and Nabi et al. \cite{NabiEtAl2024SemiparametricSensitivity} develop adjacent smooth sensitivity inference.  The regular active branch here reduces to an ordinary Gaussian normal-displacement law, whereas uniform Hausdorff inference for moving algebraic ties, collisions, continua, and order-\(k\) contacts is not supplied by those results.  Manski \cite{Manski1990TreatmentResponse} is recovered only in the joint infinite-budget limit with vanishing latent positivity.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The sharp population envelope and the general fixed-input and parametric semialgebraic procedures are separate from the worked rational witness.  The strict-gap claim relies on a deterministic exact artifact that must expose the complete stationary polynomials, Sturm chains or equivalent isolators, legal-cell inventory, denominator saturations, and objective enclosure for every competitor; neighborhood strictness then follows from continuity of compact optimized values, not from unverified persistence of one named branch.  The inference theorem is pointwise and assumes strictly positive observed cells, finite interior budgets, one unique analytic active branch, an invertible stationary Jacobian, nonzero denominators, strict inactive inequalities and objective separation, an asymptotically linear observed-summary estimator, and \(\nabla_\gamma L\neq0\).  It does not establish uniform coverage at ties, legal-root collisions, stationary continua, or order-\(k\) contacts, where the sharp Hausdorff rate and leading law remain open.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The population target is the ATE identified set for the paper's explicitly defined common-binary-confounder class, not for every model historically called a Rosenbaum--Rubin sensitivity model.  The historical citation supports only the binary-logistic fixed-tuple recalculation used as a coordinate check; it does not establish the paper's bounded union, arbitrary coupling, closure, or sharp envelope.  Endpoint attainment is over the closed finite-simplex class; over the strictly positive chart only infima, suprema, and closure are asserted unless an optimizer is interior.  The separate-pair interval is an internal outer relaxation, and strict tightening is asserted only through the complete exact witness artifact and continuity of the optimized values.  Sampling inference is proved pointwise on a unique nondegenerate active branch, with normal-displacement constant \(\sigma_L/\|\nabla_\gamma L\|\).  Uniformly honest frontier inference at optimizer ties, root collisions, positive-dimensional stationary sets, and higher-order algebraic contacts is an explicit open question.  The model retains one binary confounder, finite categorical \(X\), and observed overlap; Manski recovery occurs only as all odds budgets diverge while latent positivity may vanish.

statement_notes.justification: At a unique nondegenerate active branch, the certified population geometry is smooth enough to yield an explicit sampling law for displacement of the sign frontier.
statement_notes.gap: Generic delta-method language does not expose the derivative through the active algebraic equations or the frontier standard-error constant \(\sigma_L/\|\nabla_\gamma L\|\).
statement_notes.consumer: Investigators whose calibrated frontier lies on a certified regular branch can report a pointwise normal uncertainty measure in the scientifically relevant budget direction.

statement_notes.justification: The regular theorem removes smooth points from the uncertainty gap; the unresolved scientific problem is honest inference when the frontier changes branch, multiplicity, dimension, or contact order.
statement_notes.gap: Pointwise directional limits do not determine the sharp uniform Hausdorff rate, limit, and leading constant for moving tied or positive-dimensional algebraic active sets, especially when even-order contact creates or destroys roots.
statement_notes.consumer: Investigators need a simultaneous confidence region for all confounding budgets preserving a sign conclusion, including local sequences near singular frontier strata.

proofs.proof_tex:
Write
\[
\Theta_I(P_{\mathrm{obs}})
=\{\tau(\widetilde P):
\widetilde P\in\mathcal M(P_{\mathrm{obs}},\Gamma_A,\Gamma_0,\Gamma_1)\}.
\]
Here \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}=\mathcal L(X,A,Y)\) is a probability law on the finite set \(\mathcal X\times\{0,1\}^2\), \(\widetilde P\) is a law on \(\mathcal X\times\{0,1\}^4\), and the target \(\tau(\widetilde P)=\widetilde E\{Y(1)-Y(0)\}\) is scalar.  The observed conditions \(\lambda_x>0\), \(0<p_x<1\), and \(0<r_{a,x}<1\), and the finite budgets \(1\leq\Gamma_A,\Gamma_0,\Gamma_1<\infty\), are used below whenever we condition, cancel a margin, or take a finite odds tilt.

Fix \(x\in\mathcal X\) and first take \(\widetilde P\in\mathcal M^\circ\).  By Assumption \(\mathrm{ass{:}consistency}\),
\[
r_{a,x}=\widetilde P\{Y(a)=1\mid A=a,X=x\}.
\]
Assumption \(\mathrm{ass{:}latent\text{-}ignorability}\) then removes \(A\) from the conditional potential-outcome risk, while the definition of \(w_{a,x}\) gives
\[
r_{a,x}
=(1-w_{a,x})\mu_{a,0,x}+w_{a,x}\mu_{a,1,x}.
\tag{1}
\]
The positivity of the four \((A,U)\)-cells permits Bayes' rule and gives
\[
\pi_x=\widetilde P(U=1\mid X=x)
=p_xw_{1,x}+(1-p_x)w_{0,x}.
\tag{2}
\]
Moreover,
\[
\frac{\zeta_{1,1,x}\zeta_{0,0,x}}
     {\zeta_{1,0,x}\zeta_{0,1,x}}
=\frac{w_{1,x}(1-w_{0,x})}
       {w_{0,x}(1-w_{1,x})}.
\tag{3}
\]
Thus Assumptions \(\mathrm{ass{:}treatment\text{-}odds\text{-}upper}\) and \(\mathrm{ass{:}treatment\text{-}odds\text{-}lower}\), after cancellation of the positive factors \(\lambda_x^2p_x(1-p_x)\), are exactly \((w_{0,x},w_{1,x})\in D_{A,x}\).

Let \(\theta_{a,x}=\operatorname{OR}(\mu_{a,1,x},\mu_{a,0,x})\).  The strictly positive chart makes this odds ratio well defined.  Cancellation of the positive \((U,X)\)-margins in Assumptions \(\mathrm{ass{:}outcome\text{-}odds\text{-}upper}\) and \(\mathrm{ass{:}outcome\text{-}odds\text{-}lower}\) gives
\[
\Gamma_a^{-1}\leq\theta_{a,x}\leq\Gamma_a.
\tag{4}
\]
Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}binary\text{-}mixture\text{-}inversion}\), applied to (1), uniquely gives
\[
\mu_{a,0,x}=\kappa(r_{a,x},w_{a,x},\theta_{a,x}),
\qquad
\mu_{a,1,x}
=\frac{\theta_{a,x}\mu_{a,0,x}}
       {1+(\theta_{a,x}-1)\mu_{a,0,x}}.
\tag{5}
\]
Using (1) and (2), a direct subtraction yields the bias-decomposition identity
\[
\begin{aligned}
\widetilde E\{Y(a)\mid X=x\}
&=(1-\pi_x)\mu_{a,0,x}+\pi_x\mu_{a,1,x}\\
&=r_{a,x}+(\pi_x-w_{a,x})(\mu_{a,1,x}-\mu_{a,0,x})\\
&=q_{a,x}(w_{0,x},w_{1,x};\theta_{a,x}).
\end{aligned}
\tag{6}
\]
Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}outcome\text{-}budget\text{-}extrema}\) optimizes (6) over (4), separately for the two arms but at the same posterior pair.  Therefore
\[
H_x^-(w_{0,x},w_{1,x})
\leq \widetilde E\{Y(1)-Y(0)\mid X=x\}
\leq H_x^+(w_{0,x},w_{1,x}).
\tag{7}
\]
Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}common\text{-}u\text{-}endpoints}\) and (3) now imply
\[
\ell_x\leq \widetilde E\{Y(1)-Y(0)\mid X=x\}\leq\upsilon_x.
\tag{8}
\]
Multiplying (8) by \(\lambda_x>0\), summing over the finite support, and using \(\sum_x\lambda_x=1\) proves
\[
L\leq\tau(\widetilde P)\leq R
\qquad(\widetilde P\in\mathcal M^\circ).
\tag{9}
\]
If \(\widetilde P\in\mathcal M\), Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}common\text{-}u\text{-}class}\) supplies \(\widetilde P_k\in\mathcal M^\circ\) with \(\widetilde P_k\to\widetilde P\) in the finite simplex.  Since \(\tau\) is linear, hence continuous, (9) passes to the limit.  This proves the outer inclusion \(\Theta_I(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\subseteq[L,R]\).

We next prove the reverse inclusion by constructing compatible laws.  In each stratum select \(d_x=(w_{0,x},w_{1,x})\in D_{A,x}\) and \(\theta_{a,x}\in[\Gamma_a^{-1},\Gamma_a]\).  Suppose first that \(0<w_{0,x},w_{1,x}<1\).  Set
\[
\begin{array}{ll}
\widetilde P(A=1,U=1\mid X=x)=p_xw_{1,x},
&\widetilde P(A=1,U=0\mid X=x)=p_x(1-w_{1,x}),\\
\widetilde P(A=0,U=1\mid X=x)=(1-p_x)w_{0,x},
&\widetilde P(A=0,U=0\mid X=x)=(1-p_x)(1-w_{0,x}).
\end{array}
\tag{10}
\]
All four entries in (10) are positive and sum to one.  Define the two risks in each arm by (5).  Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}binary\text{-}mixture\text{-}inversion}\) puts all four risks in \((0,1)\) and makes (1) hold exactly.  Conditional on \((X=x,U=u)\), draw \(Y(0)\) and \(Y(1)\) independently as Bernoulli variables with success probabilities \(\mu_{0,u,x}\) and \(\mu_{1,u,x}\), and use that same conditional law at both values of \(A\).  This gives
\[
(Y(0),Y(1))\perp A\mid(X,U)
\tag{11}
\]
and makes every conditional potential-outcome cell positive.  Finally set \(Y=AY(1)+(1-A)Y(0)\).  Equations (1), (10), and consistency reproduce the observed \((A,Y)\)-law in stratum \(x\); (3), membership of \(d_x\) in \(D_{A,x}\), and (4) verify all four odds inequalities.  With \(\widetilde P(X=x)=\lambda_x\), these stratum constructions combine to a law in \(\mathcal M^\circ\), and (6) gives its arm means.

For finite \(\Gamma_A\), a point of \(D_{A,x}\) having a zero coordinate must be \((0,0)\), and a point having a unit coordinate must be \((1,1)\); this follows immediately by inserting that coordinate into the two defining inequalities of \(D_{A,x}\).  Approximate these two constant-\(U\) corners by \((\varepsilon,\varepsilon)\) and \((1-\varepsilon,1-\varepsilon)\), respectively.  These diagonal pairs lie in \(D_{A,x}\cap(0,1)^2\) for every \(0<\varepsilon<1/2\).  The laws just constructed are strictly positive, and Proposition \(\mathrm{prop{:}closed\text{-}chart\text{-}extension}\) shows that their arm means converge to the prescribed corner values.  Compactness of the finite simplex supplies a convergent subsequence; its limit has the required observed margin, belongs to \(\mathcal M\) by Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}common\text{-}u\text{-}class}\), and realizes the limiting contrast.  Thus every point in the parameter domain
\[
\mathcal D_x=D_{A,x}\times
[\Gamma_0^{-1},\Gamma_0]\times[\Gamma_1^{-1},\Gamma_1]
\tag{12}
\]
has an attaining law in \(\mathcal M\).

It remains to show that the attainable values fill the interval rather than merely attain its endpoints.  On \((0,1)^2\), the logit map sends \(D_{A,x}\) to
\[
\{(s_0,s_1)\in\mathbb R^2:|s_1-s_0|\leq\log\Gamma_A\},
\tag{13}
\]
which is convex.  Its inverse image is connected, and adjoining the two diagonal limit corners preserves connectedness.  Hence \(D_{A,x}\), and therefore \(\mathcal D_x\), is connected and compact.  The contrast map on (12) is continuous by Proposition \(\mathrm{prop{:}closed\text{-}chart\text{-}extension}\).  Its image is consequently a compact interval.  Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}outcome\text{-}budget\text{-}extrema}\) says that its minimum and maximum are precisely \(\ell_x\) and \(\upsilon_x\).  The finite product \(\prod_x\mathcal D_x\) is connected, and the weighted-sum map is continuous, so its image is the interval
\[
\left[\sum_x\lambda_x\ell_x,\sum_x\lambda_x\upsilon_x\right]=[L,R].
\tag{14}
\]
The construction following (10) attaches a law in \(\mathcal M\) to every value in (14).  Thus \([L,R]\subseteq\Theta_I(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\), which together with (9) proves sharpness.

Because \(\mathcal M=\operatorname{cl}\mathcal M^\circ\), every endpoint-attaining closed-class law is the limit of laws in \(\mathcal M^\circ\).  Continuity of \(\tau\) therefore gives
\[
\inf_{\widetilde P\in\mathcal M^\circ}\tau(\widetilde P)=L,
\qquad
\sup_{\widetilde P\in\mathcal M^\circ}\tau(\widetilde P)=R,
\qquad
\operatorname{cl}\tau(\mathcal M^\circ)=[L,R].
\tag{15}
\]
The construction is itself in \(\mathcal M^\circ\) whenever its complete full-data table is strictly positive.  Finally, the fixed-tuple calculation used here is exactly equations (1), (2), (5), and (6).  No equality or inclusion between the maintained bounded class and a historically published class is used in, or follows from, this proof.

For a stratum \(x\), abbreviate a posterior pair by \(d\in D_{A,x}\).  For every such \(d\),
\[
q^-_{1,x}(d)-q^+_{0,x}(d)
\geq \min_{e\in D_{A,x}}q^-_{1,x}(e)
-\max_{f\in D_{A,x}}q^+_{0,x}(f).
\tag{16}
\]
Taking the minimum of the left side over \(d\), multiplying by \(\lambda_x>0\), and summing proves \(L\geq L_{\mathrm{sep}}\).  Similarly,
\[
q^+_{1,x}(d)-q^-_{0,x}(d)
\leq \max_{e\in D_{A,x}}q^+_{1,x}(e)
-\min_{f\in D_{A,x}}q^-_{0,x}(f),
\tag{17}
\]
so \(R\leq R_{\mathrm{sep}}\).  Theorem \(\mathrm{thm{:}sharp\text{-}common\text{-}u\text{-}envelope}\) identifies the common-pair interval, while Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}separate\text{-}pair\text{-}relaxation}\) defines the armwise outer relaxation.  Equations (16)--(17) therefore give
\[
L_{\mathrm{sep}}\leq L\leq R\leq R_{\mathrm{sep}},
\qquad
\mathcal I_{\mathrm{com}}\subseteq\mathcal I_{\mathrm{sep}}.
\tag{18}
\]

We next verify that the law named in Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}rational\text{-}witness}\) is feasible.  Its marginal confounder prevalence and treatment odds ratio are
\[
\pi=\frac12\frac45+\frac12\frac15=\frac12,
\qquad
\operatorname{OR}\left(\frac45,\frac15\right)
=\frac{(4/5)(4/5)}{(1/5)(1/5)}=16.
\tag{19}
\]
The two observed arm risks and outcome odds ratios are
\[
\begin{aligned}
r_1&=\frac45\frac{13}{20}+\frac15\frac1{20}=\frac{53}{100},
&\theta_1&=\frac{(13/20)(19/20)}{(1/20)(7/20)}=\frac{247}{7}<36,\\
r_0&=\frac15\frac45+\frac45\frac1{10}=\frac6{25},
&\theta_0&=\frac{(4/5)(9/10)}{(1/10)(1/5)}=36.
\end{aligned}
\tag{20}
\]
Bayes' rule gives \(P^\star(A=1\mid U=1)=4/5\) and \(P^\star(A=1\mid U=0)=1/5\).  These probabilities and every displayed outcome risk lie strictly between zero and one.  Drawing the two potential outcomes independently conditional on \(U\), as specified in Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}rational\text{-}witness}\), makes every full-data cell positive and gives \((Y(0),Y(1))\perp A\mid U\).  Equations (19)--(20) verify all sensitivity inequalities.  Thus \(P^\star\in\mathcal M^\circ\), and
\[
\tau(P^\star)
=\frac12\left(\frac{13}{20}+\frac1{20}-\frac45-\frac1{10}\right)
=-\frac1{10},
\qquad
r_1-r_0=\frac{29}{100}.
\tag{21}
\]

It remains to validate the exact endpoint transcript rather than taking its construction as proof.  On the reverse arc in (C8), \(w_0=W(t)>t=w_1\), and
\[
w_0(1-w_1)=16w_1(1-w_0),
\qquad
16w_0(1-w_1)-w_1(1-w_0)=255w_1(1-w_0)>0.
\tag{22}
\]
Since \(p=1/2\), \(\pi-w_1=(W-t)/2>0\) and \(\pi-w_0=(t-W)/2<0\).  Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}outcome\text{-}budget\text{-}extrema}\) therefore makes the common lower branch \(J_{1/36}\) and the common upper branch \(J_{36}\), exactly as recorded in (C1)--(C2).

We first rule out missing interior extrema without appealing to numerical branch persistence.  For fixed \(r\in(0,1)\) and \(\vartheta>0\), let \(z(w)\) be the feasible mixture root, \(f(z)=\vartheta z/\{1+(\vartheta-1)z\}\), and \(\delta(w)=f\{z(w)\}-z(w)\).  Differentiating \(r=z+w\delta\), which is legal because
\[
D(w)=1-w+wf'\{z(w)\}>0,
\]
gives
\[
z'(w)=-\frac{\delta(w)}{D(w)},
\qquad
\delta(w)+w\delta'(w)=\frac{\delta(w)}{D(w)},
\qquad
\delta(w)-(1-w)\delta'(w)=\frac{\delta(w)f'\{z(w)\}}{D(w)}.
\tag{23}
\]
If \(\vartheta>1\), then \(\delta>0\), so (23) implies
\[
-\frac{\delta(w)}{w}<\delta'(w)<\frac{\delta(w)}{1-w}
\qquad(0<w<1).
\tag{24}
\]
On \(\mathcal I_R\), put \(e=w_0-w_1>0\) and \(S=\delta_1(w_1)+\delta_0(w_0)>0\).  The upper common objective is \(29/100+eS/2\).  By (24), \(e<w_0\) and \(e<1-w_1\) imply
\[
\frac{\partial}{\partial w_0}\left(\frac{eS}{2}\right)
=\frac{S+e\delta_0'(w_0)}2>\frac{\delta_1(w_1)}2>0,
\]
and
\[
\frac{\partial}{\partial w_1}\left(\frac{eS}{2}\right)
=\frac{-S+e\delta_1'(w_1)}2<-\frac{\delta_0(w_0)}2<0.
\tag{25}
\]
Thus there is no interior stationary point.  For \(0<\vartheta<1\), apply the same argument to \(-\delta>0\); the lower objective strictly decreases as the posterior separation is enlarged and again has no interior stationary point.  Complementing \(U\) proves the same facts on \(\mathcal I_F\).  The separate objectives are even simpler: on \(\mathcal I_R\), their derivatives in the opposite arm's posterior coordinate are the nonzero quantities \(\pm\delta_a/2\).  Hence their relevant extrema also lie on the two arcs, diagonal, or corners.  This proves that (C8) is not merely a listed set of cells but an exhaustive candidate reduction.

For the remaining one-dimensional candidates, (C2) is the implicit-differentiation numerator obtained from the two mixture equations; (23) shows that the factors \(\partial F_a/\partial z_a\) cannot vanish at a feasible root.  The resultant identity defining (C3)--(C4) therefore shows that every legal arc stationary point has \(g_-(t)=0\) or \(g_+(t)=0\).  The deterministic Sturm recurrence stated before (C5), together with the variation differences \(8-6=2\), proves that each polynomial has exactly two roots in \((0,1)\).  The four one-unit variation drops in (C5) isolate all four roots.  Substitution into the original systems, the nonzero Jacobian enclosures (C7), the legal-risk checks following (C7), and interval Newton contraction validate one and only one legal stationary triple in each box.  Thus no resultant root is missed, duplicated, or admitted through a cleared denominator.

The diagonal and corner objective is exactly \(29/100\).  Comparing this value and all four enclosures in (C6) proves
\[
L\in[-107500302/10^9,-107500301/10^9],
\qquad
R\in[539509967/10^9,539509968/10^9].
\tag{26}
\]
Theorem \(\mathrm{thm{:}complete\text{-}semialgebraic\text{-}certificate}\) justifies the exact resultant, Sturm, saturation, and interval-Newton operations used by this fixed-input transcript; the preceding cell argument and the complete coefficients and sign data in \(\mathcal C^\star\) supply its independently checkable input and output.

For the separate extrema, (C9) is obtained by the same exact implicit differentiation and elimination.  The sole additional resultant root lying in \((0,1)\), \(t=9/325\), forces \(z_0=414/395>1\) and is therefore rejected by Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}binary\text{-}mixture\text{-}inversion}\); all remaining extra factors have roots outside \((0,1)\).  Direct rational substitution of the four legal records in (C10), followed by comparison with the endpoint values in the certificate, gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
L_{\mathrm{sep}}
&=\frac{94711}{277400}-\frac{2553}{5650}
=-\frac{3461701}{31346200}
\in[-110434471/10^9,-110434470/10^9],\\
R_{\mathrm{sep}}
&=\frac{212689}{302600}-\frac{1797}{12475}
=\frac{84380923}{150997400}
\in[558823681/10^9,558823682/10^9].
\end{aligned}
\tag{27}
\]
Exact interval subtraction of (26)--(27) yields
\[
L-L_{\mathrm{sep}}
\in[2934168/10^9,2934170/10^9],
\qquad
R_{\mathrm{sep}}-R
\in[19313713/10^9,19313715/10^9].
\tag{28}
\]
Both inclusions in (18) are consequently strict at the witness.

Finally we prove open-set strictness from value-function continuity, without assuming persistence of any active algebraic branch.  Let \(\gamma\) vary near \(16\).  For an interior pair write \(s_a=\operatorname{logit}(w_a)\).  The exposure region is \(|s_1-s_0|\leq\log\gamma\).  Given \(\gamma_n\to\gamma\) and a pair in \(D_\gamma\), keep \((s_0+s_1)/2\) fixed and truncate \(s_1-s_0\) to \([-\log\gamma_n,\log\gamma_n]\); the inverse-logit pairs then lie in \(D_{\gamma_n}\) and converge to the original pair.  The two constant corners belong to every \(D_\gamma\).  Conversely, every limit of \(d_n\in D_{\gamma_n}\) satisfies the two weak polynomial inequalities for \(D_\gamma\).  Hence
\[
d_H(D_{\gamma_n},D_\gamma)\longrightarrow0,
\tag{29}
\]
where \(d_H\) is Hausdorff distance on the compact square.

Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}binary\text{-}mixture\text{-}inversion}\) and Proposition \(\mathrm{prop{:}closed\text{-}chart\text{-}extension}\) make every endpoint objective jointly continuous in \((p,r_0,r_1,\Gamma_A,\Gamma_0,\Gamma_1,d)\) near the witness; reciprocal budgets are continuous because all budgets remain positive.  To see continuity of a minimum directly, choose minimizers \(d_n\in D_{\gamma_n}\).  Compactness gives a convergent subsequence, (29) places its limit in \(D_\gamma\), and joint continuity gives the lower limit inequality.  Approximating any minimizer in \(D_\gamma\) by pairs in \(D_{\gamma_n}\), again using (29), gives the upper limit inequality.  Maxima follow by negating the objective.  The same argument applies separately to the four armwise extrema.  Thus \(L-L_{\mathrm{sep}}\) and \(R_{\mathrm{sep}}-R\) are continuous functions of the interior observed summaries and finite budgets at the witness.  Their strictly positive lower bounds in (28) remain positive on a sufficiently small relatively open neighborhood.  This proves the asserted stable strict tightening.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed: The ATE identified set over the closed class \(\mathcal M(P_{\mathrm{obs}},\Gamma_A,\Gamma_0,\Gamma_1)\) is exactly \(\mathcal I_{\mathrm{com}}=[L,R]\), with \(L\) and \(R\) defined by one common \((w_{0,x},w_{1,x})\in D_{A,x}\) per stratum.  Every endpoint is attained by a law in \(\mathcal M\): at an interior selected pair the law uses the selected feasible risks as conditional Bernoulli marginals and any coupling of \((Y(0),Y(1))\) given \((X,U)\), while a constant-\(U\) boundary pair is attained as the finite-simplex limit of such strictly positive laws.  Over \(\mathcal M^{\circ}\), \(\inf\tau=L\), \(\sup\tau=R\), and the closure of the identified set is \([L,R]\); endpoint attainment is asserted there only when an attaining law is itself strictly positive.  The result is a theorem about the maintained common-binary-confounder class and does not assert that this bounded class, its arbitrary conditional potential-outcome coupling, or its finite-simplex closure is the class defined in Rosenbaum--Rubin Sections 2--4.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The sharp envelope and attainment claim are unchanged, but the final historical sentence is too strong: the supplied Rosenbaum--Rubin record supports a fixed binary-confounder sensitivity calculation, not equality of that published formulation with this paper's arm-specific two-sided budgets, arbitrary conditional coupling of both potential outcomes, or finite-simplex closure.  The corrected claim retains the proved fixed-class theorem and expressly disclaims the unsupported class equivalence.  Because the supplied record does not establish whether the historical class uses merely armwise ignorability or a stricter common response restriction, no unverified ATE-projection transfer to a class labeled Rosenbaum--Rubin is asserted.

proposed_definition_changes.reason: The previous construction recorded only leading and constant coefficients, two isolating sign strings, and an unexpanded assertion about all competitors.  The corrected certificate gives the full stationary systems, both complete degree-sixteen factors, a deterministic definition of every Sturm chain, all root-isolating sign records, interval-Newton and Jacobian boxes, the complete legal-cell inventory, every common-pair competitor enclosure, all four separate-pair elimination factorizations, and the explicit infeasible-root rejection.

proposed.statement: The ATE identified set over the closed class \(\mathcal M(P_{\mathrm{obs}},\Gamma_A,\Gamma_0,\Gamma_1)\) is exactly \(\mathcal I_{\mathrm{com}}=[L,R]\), with \(L\) and \(R\) defined by one common \((w_{0,x},w_{1,x})\in D_{A,x}\) per stratum.  Every endpoint is attained by a law in \(\mathcal M\): at an interior selected pair the law uses the selected feasible risks as conditional Bernoulli marginals and any coupling of \((Y(0),Y(1))\) given \((X,U)\), while a constant-\(U\) boundary pair is attained as the finite-simplex limit of such strictly positive laws.  Over \(\mathcal M^{\circ}\), \(\inf\tau=L\), \(\sup\tau=R\), and the closure of the identified set is \([L,R]\); endpoint attainment is asserted there only when an attaining law is itself strictly positive.  The result is a theorem about the maintained common-binary-confounder class and does not assert that this bounded class, its arbitrary conditional potential-outcome coupling, or its finite-simplex closure is the class defined in Rosenbaum--Rubin Sections 2--4.
proposed.justification: This is the sharp population kernel: both potential-outcome arms must be simultaneously realizable through the same latent confounder.
proposed.gap: Rosenbaum--Rubin evaluate fixed sensitivity tuples; Ciocănea-Teodorescu--Gabriel--Sjölander use distinct exposure-standardization parameters; and Dorn--Guo prove sharpness for a different propensity-only model.  None gives this closed bounded common-binary-\(U\) iff envelope.
proposed.consumer: Investigators using interpretable binary-confounder calibrations obtain the narrowest logically valid ATE interval rather than an armwise diagnostic envelope.

proposed_core_edits.reason: Carry the narrowed historical scope and remove the obsolete dependency on the overnamed Rosenbaum--Rubin class-equivalence proposition; the proof derives boundary approximation directly from the class closure and the closed-chart extension.
